title.zh: 卷九十三 晉書19: 列傳八 盧質 李專美 盧詹 崔梲 薛融 曹國珍 張仁愿 趙熙 李遐 尹玉羽 鄭雲叟
title.en: Volume 93 Book of Later Jin 19: Biographies 8 - Lu Zhi, Li Zhuanmei, Lu zhan, Cui Zhuo, Xue Rong, Cao Guozhen, Zhang Renyuan, Zhao Xi, Li Xia, Yin Yuyu, Zheng Yunsou
title.raw: 卷九十三 晉書19: 列傳八 盧質 李專美 盧詹 崔梲 薛融 曹國珍 張仁愿 趙熙 李遐 尹玉羽 鄭雲叟 Volume 93 Book of Later Jin 19: Biographies 8 - Lu Zhi, Li Zhuanmei, Lu zhan, Cui Zhuo, Xue Rong, Cao Guozhen, Zhang Renyuan, Zhao Xi, Li Xia, Yin Yuyu, Zheng Yunsou

sentences.zh: 盧質，字子徵，河南人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, style Zizheng, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, styled Zizheng, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖偲，唐太原府祁縣尉，累贈右僕射。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Si was magistrate of Qi County in Taiyuan Prefecture of Tang, and was repeatedly granted posthumous honors up to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Si had served as magistrate of Qi County in the Tang Taiyuan Prefecture and was posthumously elevated on several occasions to Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 祖衍，唐刑部侍郎、太子賓客，累贈太保。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was Vice Minister of Justice and Advisor to the Crown Prince of Tang, and was repeatedly granted posthumous honors up to Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had held the Tang posts of Vice Minister of Justice and Advisor to the Crown Prince and was posthumously elevated on several occasions to Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 父望，唐尚書司勛郎中，累贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: His father Wang was Secretary of the Ministry of Personnel in the Tang Secretariat, and was repeatedly granted posthumous honors up to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang had served as Secretary in the Tang Ministry of Personnel and was posthumously elevated on several occasions to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 質幼聰慧，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zhi was clever from childhood and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Zhi was bright and gifted at writing.

sentences.zh: 年十六，陜帥王重盈奏授芮城令，能以色養。

translations.literal: At age sixteen, the military commissioner of Shaanxi, Wang Chongying, memorialized to appoint him magistrate of Ruicheng; he was able to support his parents with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he was appointed magistrate of Ruicheng on the recommendation of the Shaanxi military commissioner Wang Chongying, and he proved himself a devoted filial son to his parents.

sentences.zh: 又為同州澄城令，從私便也。

translations.literal: He also served as magistrate of Chengcheng in Tong Prefecture, following personal convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Chengcheng in Tong Prefecture, a post chosen for its proximity to home.

sentences.zh: 秩滿改秘書郎，丁母憂，歸河南故裏。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was transferred to Secretary; he entered mourning for his mother and returned to his old home in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was reassigned as a secretary, but after his mother died he went into mourning and returned to his family home in Henan.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，北遊太原，時李襲吉在武皇幕府，以女妻之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou he traveled north to Taiyuan; at that time Li Xiji was in Emperor Wu's staff headquarters and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianyou he traveled north to Taiyuan, where Li Xiji, then serving on Emperor Wu's staff, gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 武皇憐其才，承制授檢校兵部郎中，充河東節度掌書記，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu admired his talent and, by provisional commission, appointed him Honorary Director in the Ministry of War, serving as secretary to the Hedong military commissioner, and granted him the crimson fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu admired his talent and, acting under provisional authority, appointed him Honorary Director in the Ministry of War and secretary to the Hedong military commissioner, conferring on him the crimson fish tally of office.

sentences.zh: 武皇厭代，其弟克寧握兵柄，有嗣襲之望，質與張承業等密謀，同立莊宗為嗣，有翊贊之功。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu passed away, his younger brother Kening held military power and had hopes of succeeding him; Zhi secretly plotted with Zhang Chengye and others to install Zhuangzong as heir together, and had merit in supporting and assisting.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu's death his younger brother Kening held the army and looked to succeed him, but Zhi secretly joined Zhang Chengye and others in installing Zhuangzong as heir, earning merit for his loyal support.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗四征，質皆從行。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong made his four campaigns, Zhi accompanied him on all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong undertook his four great campaigns, Zhi accompanied him on every one.

sentences.zh: 十六年，轉節度判官、檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to military commissioner adjutant and Honorary Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to adjutant to the military commissioner and Honorary Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十九年，莊宗將即帝位，命為大禮使，累加至銀青光祿大夫、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, as Zhuangzong was about to ascend the throne, he was appointed Commissioner of Grand Rituals and was repeatedly promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, as Zhuangzong prepared to take the throne, he was named Commissioner of Grand Rituals and was successively promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授行臺禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of Rites of the Field Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of Rites of the field secretariat.

sentences.zh: 莊宗既登極，欲相之，質性疏逸，不喜居高位，固辭獲免。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong had ascended the throne, he wished to make him chief minister; Zhi's nature was relaxed and unfettered, and he did not like holding high office, so he firmly declined and was excused.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhuangzong had taken the throne he wished to make Zhi chief minister, but Zhi's easy, retiring temperament made him unwilling to hold high office, and his firm refusal won him release from the appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼太原尹，充北京留守事，未赴任，改戶部尚書、知制誥，充翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was given his existing rank concurrently as prefect of Taiyuan and charged with northern capital garrison duties, but before taking up the post he was transferred to Minister of Revenue, drafter of edicts, and Chief Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also named prefect of Taiyuan and charged with guarding the northern capital, but before he could take up the post he was reassigned as Minister of Revenue, drafter of edicts, and Chief Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 同光元年冬，從平大梁，權判租庸事，逾月隨駕都洛，旋受詔權知汴州軍府事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tongguang he followed the pacification of Daliang and was temporarily put in charge of land-tax and corvée affairs; after more than a month he accompanied the imperial procession to Luoyang, and soon received an edict to serve temporarily as administrator of the Bianzhou military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Tongguang he followed the campaign that pacified Daliang and was temporarily put in charge of land-tax and corvée affairs; a month later he accompanied the court to Luoyang and was soon ordered to administer the military headquarters at Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時孔謙握利權，志在聚斂，累移文於汴，配民放絲，質堅論之，事雖不行，時論賞之。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Qian held profitable power and aimed at accumulation and extraction; he repeatedly sent documents to Bian ordering the populace levied for silk collection; Zhi argued against it firmly; though the matter was not carried out, contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kong Qian held the reins of fiscal power and was intent on squeezing revenue from every source; he repeatedly sent orders to Bian demanding that the people be levied for silk collection. Zhi argued against this resolutely. Though the policy was not adopted, public opinion applauded him.

sentences.zh: 俄又改金紫光祿大夫、兵部尚書、知制誥、翰林學士承旨，仍賜論思匡佐功臣。

translations.literal: Before long he was again transferred to Golden-Purple Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of War, drafter of edicts, and Chief Hanlin Academician, and was also granted the title of Meritorious Minister Who Deliberates and Assists.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted again to Golden-Purple Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of War, drafter of edicts, and Chief Hanlin Academician, and was also granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Deliberates and Assists.

sentences.zh: 會覆試進士，質以「後從諫則聖」為賦題，以「堯、舜、禹、湯傾心求過」為韻，舊例賦韻四平四側，質所出韻乃五平三側，由是大為識者所誚。

translations.literal: When the jinshi candidates were re-examined, Zhi set the examination essay topic as "If one later follows remonstrance, then one is sage," with the rhyme words "Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang wholeheartedly seek their faults"; by old precedent examination rhyme required four level tones and four oblique tones, but the rhymes Zhi set were five level and three oblique, and for this he was greatly ridiculed by the knowledgeable.
translations.idiomatic: When the jinshi candidates came up for re-examination, Zhi set the essay topic "He who later heeds remonstrance is sage," with the rhyme phrase "Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang wholeheartedly seek their faults." By established precedent an examination rhyme scheme required four level tones and four oblique tones, but the scheme Zhi devised had five level and three oblique tones, and for this he was widely mocked by those in the know.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，制授特進、檢校司空、同州節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed by edict as Special Advancement, Honorary Minister of Works, and military commissioner of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed by imperial edict Special Advancement, Honorary Minister of Works, and military commissioner of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時宰相馮道以詩餞別，其警句云：「視草北來唐學士，擁旄西去漢將軍。

translations.literal: At that time the chief minister Feng Dao wrote a farewell poem, whose striking lines read: "A Tang academician coming north to draft edicts, a Han general going west bearing the commander's banner.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chief Minister Feng Dao composed a farewell poem whose memorable lines ran: "A Tang academician coming north to draft edicts, a Han general going west bearing the commander's banner.

sentences.zh: 」儒者榮之。

translations.literal: " Confucian scholars took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: " Confucian scholars regarded this as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 明年，改賜耀忠匡定保節功臣，就加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted the title of Meritorious Minister Who Glorifies Loyalty, Rectifies and Stabilizes, and Preserves Integrity, and was promoted on the spot to Honorary Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Glorifies Loyalty, Rectifies and Stabilizes, and Preserves Integrity, and was promoted on the spot to Honorary Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 三年，入拜兵部尚書，判太僕卿事。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered court and was appointed Minister of War, with concurrent charge of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was summoned to court as Minister of War and given concurrent charge of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 四年，進封開國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke Who Founds the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Duke Who Founds the State.

sentences.zh: 長興二年，授檢校太保、河陽節度使，未幾，移鎮滄州，入為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing he was appointed Honorary Grand Mentor and military commissioner of Heyang; before long he was transferred to command at Cangzhou, then entered court as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changxing he was appointed Honorary Grand Mentor and military commissioner of Heyang; before long he was transferred to Cangzhou, then recalled to court as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 及秦王得罪，奉詔權知河南府事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin fell from favor, he received an edict to serve temporarily as administrator of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin fell from favor, he was ordered to serve temporarily as administrator of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 應順初，遷檢校太傅，正拜河南尹，後改太子少師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun he was transferred to Honorary Grand Preceptor, formally appointed prefect of Henan, and later changed to Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yingshun he was promoted to Honorary Grand Preceptor and formally appointed prefect of Henan, and was later reassigned as Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，復為右僕射。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai he again became Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Qingtai reign he was again appointed Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，質以微恙分司洛宅。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zhi, owing to a minor illness, served in a nominal post at his Luoyang residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Zhi retired to a nominal post at his Luoyang residence on account of a minor illness.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，拜太子太保。

translations.literal: When Shaodi succeeded to the throne, he was appointed Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaodi succeeded to the throne, Zhi was appointed Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 天福七年秋，卒於洛陽，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu he died in Luoyang, at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu he died in Luoyang at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 累贈太子太師，謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly granted posthumous honors up to Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince, and was given the posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously elevated on several occasions to Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince and was given the posthumous title Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：漢乾祐元年九月，其子尚書兵部員外郎盧瓊上章請謚，下太常議，謚曰文忠。）〉

translations.literal: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties: In the ninth month of the first year of Qianyou of Han, his son Lu Qiong, Secretary in the Ministry of War, submitted a memorial requesting a posthumous title; the matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for deliberation, and the posthumous title Wenzhong was granted.)]
translations.idiomatic: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties records that in the ninth month of the first year of Qianyou of Han, his son Lu Qiong, Secretary in the Ministry of War, submitted a memorial requesting a posthumous title; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was consulted, and the posthumous title Wenzhong was granted.)]

sentences.zh: 子十一人，唯第六子夏，仕至省郎，余歷州縣焉。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons; only the sixth, Xia, rose to a secretariat secretary, while the rest served in prefectural and county posts.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons. Only the sixth, Xia, rose to serve as a secretariat secretary; the rest held posts in prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 李專美，字翊商，京兆萬年人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhuanmei, style Yishang, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhuanmei, styled Yishang, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖隨，光祿卿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Sui was Director of the Imperial Household for Food.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sui had served as Director of the Imperial Household for Food.

sentences.zh: 祖正範，尚書庫部郎中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhengfan was Secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhengfan had served as Secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 專美少篤學文，以父樞唐昭宗時常應進士舉，為覆試所落，不許再入，專美心愧之，由是不遊文場。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei from youth devoted himself to learning and letters; because his father Shu during Emperor Zhaozong of Tang had repeatedly entered the jinshi examination and was failed in the re-examination and not permitted to enter again, Zhuanmei felt ashamed in his heart, and for this reason did not enter the literary arena.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei from youth devoted himself to learning and letters. His father Shu had repeatedly taken the jinshi examination under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang, only to be failed in the re-examination and barred from trying again. Zhuanmei was deeply ashamed of this and therefore never entered the examination halls himself.

sentences.zh: 偽梁貞明中，河南尹張全義以專美名族之後，奏為陸渾尉，秩滿，改舞陽令。

translations.literal: In the Zhenming era of the false Liang, the Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi, because Zhuanmei was descended from a famous clan, memorialized to appoint him sheriff of Luhun; when his term expired he was transferred to magistrate of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenming era of the Later Liang, the Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi, recognizing Zhuanmei as scion of a distinguished clan, recommended him as sheriff of Luhun; when his term expired he was transferred to magistrate of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 專美性廉謹，大著政聲。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei was by nature incorrupt and careful, and greatly distinguished himself in administrative reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei was incorruptible and conscientious by nature, and earned a strong reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成中，安邑榷鹽使李肅辟為推官，時唐末帝鎮河中，見其敦雅，心重之。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, the salt monopoly commissioner of Anyi, Li Su, recruited him as investigating officer; at that time the Last Emperor of Tang was stationed at Hezhong, saw his earnest refinement, and held him in high regard in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, Li Su, the salt monopoly commissioner of Anyi, recruited him as investigating officer. The Last Emperor of Tang was then stationed at Hezhong, and when he saw Zhuanmei's earnest refinement he came to hold him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 末帝一日曾召肅宴於衙署，專美亦預坐，末帝謂肅曰：「某夜來夢主上召去，與宋王同剃卻頭，何也？

translations.literal: One day the Last Emperor summoned Su to a banquet in the yamen, and Zhuanmei also took a seat; the Last Emperor said to Su: "Last night I dreamed that the sovereign summoned me away and that I shaved my head together with the Prince of Song—what does this mean?
translations.idiomatic: One day the Last Emperor summoned Su to a banquet at his headquarters, with Zhuanmei also in attendance. The Last Emperor said to Su: "Last night I dreamed that the sovereign summoned me and that the Prince of Song and I shaved our heads together. What could this mean?

sentences.zh: 」坐客都無對者，專美屏人謂曰：「將來必為嗣主。

translations.literal: " All the seated guests had no reply; Zhuanmei, sending others aside, said to him: "In the future you will surely become the succeeding sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: " None of those present could answer. Zhuanmei drew him aside and said: "You will surely become the heir to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」由是愈重焉。

translations.literal: " From this he valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " From that point on the Last Emperor valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 末帝留守長安，奏為從事，及移鎮鳳翔，遷為記室。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor remained to guard Chang'an, he memorialized to appoint him staff officer; when he was transferred to garrison Fengxiang, Zhuanmei was promoted to recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor was left to guard Chang'an he had Zhuanmei appointed as a staff officer, and when he was transferred to Fengxiang he promoted him to recorder.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，除尚書庫部郎中，賜金紫，充樞密院直學士。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, he was appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Works, granted the gold-and-purple insignia, and appointed Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor took the throne he appointed Zhuanmei Secretary in the Ministry of Works, granted him the gold-and-purple insignia, and made him Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，末帝起自鳳翔，大許諸軍厚賞。

translations.literal: At first, when the Last Emperor rose from Fengxiang, he greatly promised the various armies generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor first rose from Fengxiang he had promised the armies lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 洎至洛陽，閱內庫金帛不過二三萬，尋又配率京城戶民，雖行捶楚，亦所獲無幾，末帝憂之。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang, he examined the inner treasury and found gold and silk amounting to no more than twenty or thirty thousand; soon afterward the households of the capital were also levied, and though whipping and beating were applied, little was obtained; the Last Emperor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Luoyang, inspection of the inner treasury showed no more than twenty or thirty thousand in gold and silk. The capital households were then levied as well, but even with whipping and beating the yield was meager, and the Last Emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 會專美宿於禁中，末帝召而讓之曰：「卿士人子弟，常言有才術，今致我至此，不能度運以濟時事，留才術何施也！

translations.literal: When Zhuanmei happened to lodge in the palace precincts, the Last Emperor summoned and reproached him, saying: "You are the son of a scholar's house and always speak of talent and skill; now you have brought me to this point and cannot measure the times to rescue current affairs—of what use is talent and skill left behind!
translations.idiomatic: One night when Zhuanmei was staying in the palace, the Last Emperor summoned and rebuked him: "You are a scholar's son and always speak of talent and ability. Yet you have brought me to this pass and cannot read the times well enough to remedy our situation. What good is talent and ability then?

sentences.zh: 」專美惶恐待罪，良久奏曰：「臣才力駑劣，屬當興運，陛下猥垂錄任，無以裨益聖朝，然府藏空竭，軍賞不給，非臣之罪也。

translations.literal: " Zhuanmei, fearful, awaited punishment; after a long while he submitted: "Your subject's talent and strength are dull and inferior; I happened to meet a rising fortune, and Your Majesty undeservedly favored me with appointment, yet I have been unable to benefit the sacred court; however, the treasury stores are empty and exhausted and army rewards cannot be supplied—this is not your subject's fault.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuanmei, terrified, awaited punishment. After a long silence he replied: "Your subject's talents are meager, and though Your Majesty undeservedly favored me at a time of rising fortune, I have been unable to serve the court effectively. Yet the treasury is empty and the army's rewards cannot be paid—this is not my fault alone.

sentences.zh: 臣思明宗棄代之際，是時府庫濫賞已竭，繼以鄂王臨朝，紀綱大壞，縱有無限之財賦，不能滿驕軍溪壑之心，所以陛下孤立岐陽而得天下。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that when Emperor Mingzong passed away, at that time the treasury had already been exhausted by indiscriminate rewards; this was followed by the Prince of E holding court, when discipline was greatly ruined; even if there had been limitless wealth and revenue, it could not have filled the insatiable hearts of the arrogant armies, and for this reason Your Majesty, isolated at Qiyang, was able to gain the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject reflects that when Emperor Mingzong died the treasury had already been drained by reckless rewards. Then the Prince of E took the throne and discipline collapsed utterly. Even limitless wealth could not have satisfied the insatiable demands of the arrogant armies. That is why Your Majesty, standing alone at Qiyang, was able to win the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣以為國之存亡，不專在行賞，須刑政立於上，恥格行於下，賞當功，罰當罪，則近於理道也。

translations.literal: Your subject believes that the survival or destruction of a state does not lie solely in granting rewards; punishments and government must be established above, and shame and reform must be practiced below; rewards must match merit and punishments must match crimes—then one approaches the way of reason.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that a state's survival does not depend on rewards alone. Punishment and governance must be established at the top, shame and reform practiced below, rewards matched to merit and punishments to crimes—only then does one approach the way of good government.

sentences.zh: 若陛下不改覆車之轍，以賞無賴之軍，徒困蒸民，存亡未可知也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not change the track of the overturned cart and uses rewards for unruly armies, you will only exhaust the common people, and survival or destruction cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not turn from the path that overturned the cart and keeps rewarding unruly soldiers, you will only grind down the common people, and whether the state survives or perishes is impossible to say.

sentences.zh: 今宜取見在財賦以給之，不必踐前言而希茍悅。

translations.literal: Now you should take the wealth and revenue presently available to supply them, and need not fulfill earlier words in hope of fawning approval.
translations.idiomatic: You should pay them from the revenue at hand and need not keep your earlier promises merely to win their favor.

sentences.zh: 」末帝然之。

translations.literal: " The Last Emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Last Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及其行賞，雖不愜於軍士，然洛陽戶民獲免鞭笞之苦，由專美之敷揚也。

translations.literal: When rewards were distributed, though the soldiers were not satisfied, the households of Luoyang were spared the suffering of whipping and beating—this was due to Zhuanmei's exposition and advocacy.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were finally distributed the soldiers were displeased, but the households of Luoyang were spared the lash—thanks to Zhuanmei's counsel.

sentences.zh: 尋轉給事中，明年，遷兵部侍郎、端明殿學士，未幾，改檢校尚書右僕射、守秘書監，充宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Supervising Censor; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance; before long he was changed to Honorary Right Vice Director in the Secretariat, Acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Supervising Censor. The following year he became Vice Minister of War and Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, and before long was reassigned Honorary Right Vice Director in the Secretariat, Acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖入洛，以例除名。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, he was removed from office by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, Zhuanmei was dismissed from office according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 三年，復授衛尉少卿，繼遷鴻臚、大理卿。

translations.literal: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard, and was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was reappointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard and was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 開運中，以病卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era he died of illness, at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyun era he died of illness at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 專美之遠祖本出姑臧大房，與清河小房崔氏、北祖第二房盧氏、昭國鄭氏為四望族，皆不以才行相尚，不以軒冕為貴，雖布衣徒步，視公卿蔑如也。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei's remote ancestors originally came from the senior branch of the Guzang Li clan, and together with the junior branch of the Qinghe Cui, the second branch of the northern Lu, and the Zhaoguo Zheng constituted the Four Eminent Clans; they all did not esteem one another for talent and conduct, did not regard carriage and cap as noble, and even in plain cloth walking on foot looked upon high ministers with disdain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei's remote ancestors came from the senior branch of the Guzang Li clan, which together with the junior branch of the Qinghe Cui, the second northern branch of the Lu, and the Zhaoguo Zheng made up the Four Eminent Clans. None of these families valued one another for talent or character, nor did they regard rank and office as marks of worth; even in plain dress on foot they looked down on the highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 男女婚嫁，不雜他姓，欲聘其族，厚贈金帛始許焉。

translations.literal: In marriage for men and women they did not mix with other surnames; those wishing to betroth into their clans had first to present generous gifts of gold and silk before consent was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In marriage they would not mix with other surnames; suitors seeking to join these clans had to offer lavish gifts of gold and silk before consent would be given.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗曾降詔以戒其弊風，終莫能改。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang once issued an edict to warn against this corrupt custom, but in the end it could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong of Tang once issued an edict condemning this corrupt custom, but it could never be changed.

sentences.zh: 其間有未達者，必曰：「姓崔、盧、李、鄭了，余復何求耶！

translations.literal: Among them, those who had not yet attained success would invariably say: "One has the surnames Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng—what more is there to seek!
translations.idiomatic: Those among them who had not yet risen in the world would say: "With the surnames Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng, what more could one want?

sentences.zh: 」其遠者，則邈在天表，敻若千里，人罕造其門，浮薄自大，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " Those who were remote stood as if beyond the heavens, distant as a thousand li; people rarely visited their gates; frivolous arrogance and self-importance—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " The more distant branches carried themselves as if beyond the heavens, remote as a thousand li; few ever crossed their thresholds. Such frivolous arrogance was typical of them all.

sentences.zh: 唯專美未嘗以氏族形於口吻，見寒素士大夫，恒恂恂如也，人以此多之。

translations.literal: Only Zhuanmei never let clan status appear on his lips; when he saw poor and plain scholar-officials he was always respectful and deferential, and people for this reason praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei alone never flaunted his clan on his lips. Toward poor and plain scholar-officials he was always respectful and deferential, and for this people held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 專美職岐下，曾夢具裳簡立嵩山之頂。

translations.literal: While Zhuanmei held office below Qi he once dreamed that he stood on the summit of Mount Song holding ceremonial robes and tablets.
translations.idiomatic: While serving below Qi, Zhuanmei once dreamed that he stood on the summit of Mount Song in full ceremonial dress holding the court tablets.

sentences.zh: 及為端明殿學士，學士李崧同列而班在其上，因以所夢告崧，且言：「某非德非勛，安可久居此位，處吾子之首乎！

translations.literal: When he became Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, the academician Li Song was of the same rank but ranked above him in precedence; he therefore told Song of his dream and also said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this position and stand above you!
translations.idiomatic: When he became Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, his colleague Li Song ranked above him in court precedence. He told Song of his dream and said: "I have neither virtue nor merit—how can I long hold this post and stand above you?

sentences.zh: 」因懇求他官，尋移宣徽使，崧深德之。

translations.literal: " He therefore earnestly requested another office, and soon was transferred to palace commissioner; Song deeply appreciated him for this.
translations.idiomatic: " He earnestly requested another post and was soon transferred to palace commissioner. Song was deeply grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖臨朝，崧為樞密使，與桑維翰同列，維翰與專美亦有舊，乃協力以奏之，遂復朝序，位至九卿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held court, Song was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and ranked together with Sang Weihan; Weihan also had old ties with Zhuanmei, and they jointly memorialized on his behalf, whereupon he was restored to court rank and rose to one of the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Song served as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs alongside Sang Weihan. Weihan also had old ties with Zhuanmei, and together they memorialized on his behalf, restoring him to court rank until he rose to one of the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 專美曾使閩中，遇風水漂至兩浙，逾歲無恙而還，至是善終，人以為神道福謙之所致也。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei had once been sent on mission to Min, encountered wind and water and was carried to the Two Zhes; after more than a year he returned unharmed; when he now died a good death, people considered it the result of the Way of spirits blessing humility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei had once been sent on mission to Min, was blown by wind and water to the Two Zhes, and returned unharmed after more than a year. When he now died peacefully, people attributed it to the spirits rewarding his humility.

sentences.zh: 崔棁，字子文，博陵安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Zhuo, style Ziwen, was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhuo, styled Ziwen, was a native of Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 累世冠冕。

translations.literal: For generations his family held official caps and posts.
translations.idiomatic: His family had held office for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖元受，舉進士，直史館。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuanshou passed the jinshi examination and served in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yuanshou had passed the jinshi examination and served in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 祖銖，安、濮二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhu was prefect of An and Pu Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhu had served as prefect of An and Pu Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 父涿，刑部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Zhuo was Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuo had served as Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 棁少好學，梁貞明三年，舉進士甲科，為開封尹王瓚從事。

translations.literal: Zhuo from youth loved learning; in the third year of Zhenming of Liang he passed the jinshi examination in the top class and became staff officer to the Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo loved learning from youth. In the third year of Zhenming of Liang he passed the jinshi examination in the top class and became a staff officer to the Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan.

sentences.zh: 棁性至孝，父涿有疾，謂親友曰：「死生有命，無醫為也。

translations.literal: Zhuo was by nature extremely filial; when his father Zhuo fell ill, he said to relatives and friends: "Life and death have their allotted span—there is no use in physicians.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was deeply filial by nature. When his father Zhuo fell ill, the father said to relatives and friends: "Life and death are fated—there is no point in calling physicians.

sentences.zh: 」棁侍之衣不解帶，有賓至，必拜泣告於門外，請方便勸其進藥，涿終莫之從。

translations.literal: " Zhuo attended him without loosening his belt day or night; when guests arrived he would bow and weep and tell them outside the gate, asking them to find an opportune moment to urge his father to take medicine, but Zhuo in the end never complied.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo attended him without ever loosening his belt. When guests arrived Zhuo would bow and weep at the gate, begging them to find a moment to urge his father to take medicine, but Zhuo the father never consented.

sentences.zh: 及丁憂，哀毀過制。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning, his grief and devastation exceeded the prescribed rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning his grief exceeded the prescribed limits.

sentences.zh: 明宗朝，授監察御史，不應命，逾年詔再下，乃就列焉。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Mingzong he was appointed Investigating Censor but did not accept the commission; after more than a year the edict was issued again, and only then did he take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Mingzong's reign he was appointed Investigating Censor but declined. More than a year later, when the edict came again, he finally accepted the post.

sentences.zh: 累遷都官郎中、翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 天福初，以戶部侍郎為學士承旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he served as Vice Minister of Revenue and Chief Academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianfu he served as Vice Minister of Revenue and Chief Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 嘗草制，為宰相桑維翰所改，棁以唐故事，學士草制有所改者，當罷職，乃引經據爭，維翰不能詰，命權知二年貢舉。

translations.literal: He once drafted an edict that was altered by the chief minister Sang Weihan; Zhuo, citing Tang precedent that when an academician's draft was altered he should be dismissed from office, cited classics and argued on evidence; Weihan could not rebut him and ordered him to serve temporarily as supervisor of the second year's civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He once drafted an edict that Chief Minister Sang Weihan altered. Citing Tang precedent that an academician whose draft was changed should be dismissed, Zhuo argued from classical authority. Weihan could not refute him and instead assigned him to supervise the second year's civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 時有進士孔英者，素有醜行，為當時所惡，棁受命往見維翰，維翰語素簡，謂棁曰：「孔英來矣。

translations.literal: At that time there was a jinshi candidate named Kong Ying who had long had disgraceful conduct and was detested by contemporaries; Zhuo, having received his commission, went to see Weihan; Weihan's words were always brief, and he said to Zhuo: "Kong Ying is coming.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a jinshi candidate named Kong Ying was notorious for disgraceful conduct and widely despised. When Zhuo received his commission and went to see Weihan, Weihan, who was always terse in speech, said to him: "Kong Ying is coming.

sentences.zh: 」棁不諭其意，以謂維翰以孔英為言，乃考英及第，物議大以為非，遂罷學士，拜尚書左丞，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: " Zhuo did not understand his meaning and thought Weihan was speaking of Kong Ying, so he passed Ying in the examination; public opinion greatly considered this wrong, and he was therefore dismissed as academician, appointed Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat, and transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo failed to grasp his meaning and thought Weihan was referring to Kong Ying, so he passed Ying in the examination. Public opinion strongly condemned this, and Zhuo was dismissed as academician, appointed Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat, and transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 後以風痹改太子賓客，分司西京。

translations.literal: Later, owing to wind paralysis, he was transferred to Advisor to the Crown Prince and served in a nominal post in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, afflicted with wind paralysis, he was reassigned Advisor to the Crown Prince and given a nominal post in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十八。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 棁平生所著文章、碑誄、制詔甚多，人有借本傳寫者，則曰：「有前賢，有來者，奚用此為！

translations.literal: Zhuo in his lifetime composed many essays, stele inscriptions, eulogies, and edicts; when people asked to borrow copies to transcribe, he would say: "There are former worthies and there are those yet to come—what use is this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo wrote many essays, stele inscriptions, eulogies, and edicts in his lifetime. When people asked to borrow copies to transcribe, he would say: "There are the sages of the past and writers yet to come—what need is there for this?

sentences.zh: 」凡受托而作者，必親劄致之，即焚其槁，懼泄人之假手也。

translations.literal: " Whenever he composed on commission, he always personally delivered the finished piece and then burned the draft, fearing that others might use his handiwork to pass off their own.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever he wrote on commission he delivered the finished piece in person and then burned the draft, fearing that others might pass off his work as their own.

sentences.zh: 棁笑不至矧，怒不至詈，接新進後生，未嘗無誨焉。

translations.literal: Zhuo's laughter never reached a grin, his anger never reached cursing; when receiving newly advanced young men he never failed to offer instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo never laughed to excess nor cursed in anger, and whenever he received newly advanced young men he always offered them guidance.

sentences.zh: 群居公會端坐寡言，嘗雲非止致人愛憎，且或幹人祖禰之諱。

translations.literal: In group gatherings and public assemblies he sat upright and spoke little, once saying that this was not only to avoid arousing love or hatred in others, but also lest one touch upon the taboo names of others' ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: At gatherings and public assemblies he sat upright and spoke little, explaining that this was not only to avoid arousing others' love or hatred but also lest one inadvertently violate the taboo names of someone's ancestors.

sentences.zh: 指命仆役，亦用禮節，盛暑祁寒，不使冒犯。

translations.literal: When directing servants he also used proper courtesy; in blazing summer and bitter cold he did not allow them to be offended or overworked.
translations.idiomatic: Even when giving orders to servants he observed proper courtesy, and in blazing heat or bitter cold he would not let them be overworked or mistreated.

sentences.zh: 嘗自話於知友云：「某少時，夢二人前引行路，一人計地裏，曰：『一舍矣，可以止。

translations.literal: He once told close friends: "When I was young I dreamed that two men walked ahead leading me on the road; one counted the distance in li and said: 'One stage already—we may stop.
translations.idiomatic: He once told close friends: "When I was young I dreamed that two men walked ahead leading me on the road. One counted the distance and said: 'One stage already—we may stop.

sentences.zh: 』一人曰：『此君當更進三十有八里。

translations.literal: ' The other said: 'This gentleman should go thirty-eight li farther.
translations.idiomatic: ' The other said: 'This gentleman must go thirty-eight li farther.

sentences.zh: 』復行如所言，二人皆止之，俄而驚覺。

translations.literal: ' They walked on as spoken, and both men stopped him; soon he awoke with a start.
translations.idiomatic: ' They walked on as directed, and both men stopped him there. Then he awoke with a start.

sentences.zh: 」棁常識是夢，以為定命之限，故六十七請退，明年果終焉。

translations.literal: " Zhuo always recognized this dream and took it as the limit of allotted fate; therefore at sixty-seven he requested retirement, and the next year he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo always took this dream as the measure of his allotted span; at sixty-seven he asked to retire, and the following year he died as the dream foretold.

sentences.zh: 兄棆，有隱德，好釋氏，閑居滑州。

translations.literal: His elder brother Lin had hidden virtue, favored Buddhism, and lived in retirement in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Lin was a man of quiet virtue who favored Buddhism and lived in retirement in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲訪人於白馬津北，及臨岸，嘆曰：「波勢洶湧如此，安可濟乎！

translations.literal: He once wished to visit someone north of the White Horse Ford, but when he came to the bank he sighed and said: "The waves are surging so violently—how can one cross!
translations.idiomatic: He once wished to visit someone north of the White Horse Ford, but when he reached the bank he sighed and said: "The waves are surging like this—how can anyone cross?

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " So he turned back.

sentences.zh: 後征拜左拾遺，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder but declined on grounds of illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned as Left Reminder but pleaded illness and declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 薛融，汾州平遙人。

translations.literal: Xue Rong was a man of Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rong was a native of Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性純和，以儒學為業。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and gentle, and he made Confucian learning his profession.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was pure and gentle, and devoted himself to Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 初從雲州帥李存璋為幕職，唐莊宗平河南，歷鄆、徐二鎮從事。

translations.literal: At first he followed the military commissioner of Yun Prefecture, Li Cunzhang, as a staff officer; when Tang Zhuangzong pacified Henan he successively served as staff officer in the Yan and Xu garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He first served on the staff of Li Cunzhang, military commissioner of Yun Prefecture. After Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Henan, he held staff posts in the Yan and Xu garrisons in turn.

sentences.zh: 明宗初，授華州節度判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingzong's reign he was appointed adjutant to the military commissioner of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Mingzong's reign he was appointed adjutant to the military commissioner of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長興四年，入為右補闕，直宏文館，歲餘，改河東觀察判官，會高祖鎮太原，遂居於幕府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing he entered court as Right Supplementation Censor and served in the Hongwen Hall; after more than a year he was transferred adjutant to the Hedong observation commissioner; when Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan he then resided in the staff headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changxing he entered court as Right Supplementation Censor and served in the Hongwen Hall. After more than a year he became adjutant to the Hedong observation commissioner, and when Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan he joined his staff.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，高祖將舉義，延賓席而歷問之，次及融，對曰：「融本儒生，只曾讀三五卷書，至於軍旅之事，進退存亡之機，未之學也。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai, as Gaozu was about to raise the banner of revolt, he spread guest seats and questioned them in turn; when it came to Rong, he replied: "Rong is originally a Confucian scholar and has read only three or five volumes of books; as for military affairs and the critical moments of advance, retreat, survival, and destruction, I have not studied them.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Qingtai, as Gaozu prepared to raise the banner of revolt, he gathered his guests and questioned them one by one. When it was Rong's turn he replied: "I am only a Confucian scholar who has read a handful of books. I know nothing of military affairs or the critical choices of advance, retreat, survival, and destruction.

sentences.zh: 」座中聳然。

translations.literal: " Those seated were startled.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone present was startled.

sentences.zh: 及登極，遷尚書吏部郎中兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Rong was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel of the Secretariat, concurrently Serving Censor with charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Rong was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently Serving Censor with charge of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，自左諫議大夫遷中書舍人，自以文學非優，不敢拜命，復為諫議。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was transferred from Left Remonstrance and Policy Advisor to Drafting Secretary of the Central Secretariat; considering his literary learning not superior, he did not dare accept the commission and again became Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu he was promoted from Left Remonstrance and Policy Advisor to Drafting Secretary of the Central Secretariat, but judging his literary gifts insufficient he declined the appointment and returned to his former post as Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.

sentences.zh: 時詔修西京大內，融以鄴下用兵，國用不足，上疏復罷之，

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered the repair of the Western Capital inner palace; Rong, because troops were deployed below Ye and state revenue was insufficient, submitted a memorial requesting that the project again be halted,
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict ordered repairs to the inner palace of the Western Capital. Because troops were engaged below Ye and state revenue was insufficient, Rong submitted a memorial asking that the project be halted again,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：薛融諫曰：「今宮室雖經焚毀，猶侈於帝堯之茅茨；

translations.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror: Xue Rong remonstrated, saying: "Though the palace halls have been burned, they are still more lavish than Emperor Yao's thatched hut;
translations.idiomatic: (The Comprehensive Mirror: Xue Rong remonstrated: "Though the palace halls have been burned, they are still more lavish than Emperor Yao's thatched hut;

sentences.zh: 所費雖寡，猶多於漢文之露臺。

translations.literal: though the expense is small, it is still greater than Emperor Wen of Han's open terrace.
translations.idiomatic: and though the expense may be modest, it still exceeds Emperor Wen of Han's open terrace.

sentences.zh: 況魏城未下，公私困窘，誠非陛下修宮館之日。

translations.literal: Moreover, Weicheng has not yet fallen and public and private resources are in distress—this is truly not the day for Your Majesty to repair palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Weicheng has not yet fallen and both public and private resources are strained—this is hardly the time for Your Majesty to repair palace halls.

sentences.zh: 俟海內平寧，修之未晚。）〉

translations.literal: Wait until the realm within the seas is peaceful and settled, and repair will not be too late.)]
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the realm is at peace, and repairs will not be too late.)]

sentences.zh: 優詔嘉許。

translations.literal: An excellent edict praised and approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with a gracious edict of approval.

sentences.zh: 俄轉御史中丞，秩滿改尚書右丞，分司西都。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief; when his term expired he was changed to Right Assistant Director in the Secretariat and served in a nominal post in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief. When his term expired he became Right Assistant Director in the Secretariat and took a nominal post in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 天福六年，以疾卒，年六十餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died of illness, at age sixty-some.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died of illness at over sixty years of age.

sentences.zh: 曹國珍，字彥輔，幽州固安人也。

translations.literal: Cao Guozhen, style Yanfu, was a man of Gu'an in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Guozhen, styled Yanfu, was a native of Gu'an in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖藹，祖蟾，父絢，代襲儒素。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ai, grandfather Chan, and father Xuan—generation after generation inherited plain Confucian virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ai, grandfather Chan, and father Xuan had passed down plain scholarly virtue for generations.

sentences.zh: 國珍少值燕薊亂離，因落發被緇，客於河西延州，高萬興兄弟皆好文，辟為從事。

translations.literal: Guozhen in youth encountered the turmoil and separation of Yan and Ji, and therefore shaved his head and donned monastic robes; he sojourned at Yan Prefecture in Hexi, where the brothers Gao Wanxing all favored letters and recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Guozhen lived through the turmoil of Yan and Ji and shaved his head to become a monk. He sojourned at Yan Prefecture in Hexi, where the Gao Wanxing brothers, all lovers of literature, recruited him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 國珍常以文章自許，求貢禮闈，且掌書奏，期年，入為左拾遺，累遷至尚書郎。

translations.literal: Guozhen often prided himself on his essays, sought to present himself for examination at the Ministry of Rites, and also managed memorials and reports; after a year he entered court as Left Reminder and was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen prided himself on his writing, sought to enter the civil examinations, and also managed memorials and reports. Within a year he entered court as Left Reminder and was successively promoted to Secretariat Secretary.

sentences.zh: 每與人交，傾財無吝。

translations.literal: Whenever he associated with others he spent his wealth freely without stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: In his dealings with others he spent his wealth freely and without stint.

sentences.zh: 性頗剛僻，經藝史學，非其所長，好自矜衒，多上章疏，文字差誤，數數有之，為縉紳所誚。

translations.literal: His nature was rather stubborn and eccentric; classical learning and historical studies were not his strengths; he liked to boast and show off; he often submitted memorials and reports, and textual errors occurred repeatedly, for which he was ridiculed by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stubborn and eccentric. Classical learning and historical scholarship were not his strengths, yet he loved to boast. He submitted memorial after memorial, and textual errors appeared again and again, drawing ridicule from the gentry.

sentences.zh: 高祖在藩時，嘗通私謁，以兄事之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was in his princely domain he once paid private visits and treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was still in his princely domain he had visited him privately and treated him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及即位，國珍自比於嚴陵，上表敘舊，由是自吏部郎中拜左諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Guozhen compared himself to Yanling, submitted a memorial recounting their old ties, and thereby was promoted from Director in the Ministry of Personnel to Left Remonstrance and Policy Advisor and Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Guozhen likened himself to Yan Guang, submitted a memorial recalling their old friendship, and was promoted from Director in the Ministry of Personnel to Left Remonstrance and Policy Advisor and Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史·張彥澤傳》：國珍與御史中丞王易簡率三院御史詣閣門，連疏論張彥澤，不報。）〉

translations.literal: (Ouyang's History, Biography of Zhang Yanze: Guozhen and the Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian led the censors of the Three Bureaus to the Gate of Audience and submitted successive memorials concerning Zhang Yanze, but received no response.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang's History, Biography of Zhang Yanze: Guozhen and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian led the censors of the Three Bureaus to the Gate of Audience and submitted successive memorials against Zhang Yanze, but received no response.)]

sentences.zh: 又求為御史中丞，時宰政不復為請，國珍銜之。

translations.literal: He also requested to become Vice Censor-in-Chief, but the chief ministers no longer petitioned on his behalf, and Guozhen harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief, but the chief ministers declined to petition on his behalf, and Guozhen nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 李崧之母薨，遣諸弟護喪歸葬深州，崧既起復，乃出北郊路隅設奠，公卿大夫皆送喪而出，國珍固爭不行，眾鹹推其讜直。

translations.literal: When Li Song's mother died, he sent his younger brothers to escort the coffin home for burial in Shen Prefecture; Song had already returned to office from mourning, yet went out to the roadside at the northern suburbs to set out offerings; high ministers and grandees all went out to escort the funeral, but Guozhen firmly argued against going and did not; the multitude all praised his forthright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Song's mother died he sent his younger brothers to escort the coffin home for burial in Shen Prefecture. Though Song had already returned to office from mourning, he went to the northern suburbs to set out offerings, and high ministers and grandees all turned out for the funeral escort. Guozhen firmly refused to go, and everyone praised his blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 高祖晏駕，朝廷以宰臣馮道為山陵使，及靈盾既發，國珍上疏言：「馮道既為山陵使，不得復入都城，請除外佐，以桑維翰入輔。

translations.literal: When Gaozu passed away, the court appointed the chief minister Feng Dao as commissioner for the imperial tomb; after the spirit shield had departed, Guozhen submitted a memorial saying: "Since Feng Dao is commissioner for the imperial tomb, he must not again enter the capital; I request that he be excluded as an outside assistant and that Sang Weihan enter to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died the court appointed Chief Minister Feng Dao commissioner for the imperial tomb. After the funeral procession had departed, Guozhen submitted a memorial saying: "Since Feng Dao serves as tomb commissioner he must not re-enter the capital. I ask that he be excluded from assisting at court and that Sang Weihan be brought in to assist instead.

sentences.zh: 李崧請罷相位，俾持喪制。

translations.literal: Li Song should be asked to relinquish the chief ministership and be allowed to observe mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song should be asked to step down from the chief ministership and observe the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 」少帝覽奏，以所言侵越，出為陜州行軍司馬。

translations.literal: " When Shaodi read the memorial he considered the words overreaching and demoted him to marching commander of Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " When Shaodi read the memorial he judged the words overreaching and demoted Guozhen to marching commander of Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至任悒怏，遘疾而卒。

translations.literal: When he reached his post he was depressed and resentful, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached his post he was depressed and resentful, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 張仁願，字善政，開封陳留人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Renyuan, style Shanzheng, was a man of Chenliu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Renyuan, styled Shanzheng, was a native of Chenliu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 祖晸，唐右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing was Great General of the Tang Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing had served as Great General of the Tang Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 父存敬，梁河中節度觀察留後，累贈中書令，《梁書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Cunjing was acting military commissioner and observation commissioner of Hezhong in Liang, repeatedly granted posthumous honors up to Director of the Central Secretariat; the Book of Liang has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cunjing had served as acting military commissioner and observation commissioner of Hezhong under the Liang and was posthumously elevated to Director of the Central Secretariat; the Book of Liang contains his biography.

sentences.zh: 仁願梁貞明初，以勛臣之子起家為衛尉寺主簿，改著作佐郎、左贊善大夫，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming of Liang, as the son of a meritorious minister Renyuan began his career as chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Guard, was changed to Assistant Editor and Left Supporter of Goodness Grandee, and was granted the crimson fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenming of Liang, as the son of a meritorious minister Renyuan began his career as chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Guard, then became Assistant Editor and Left Supporter of Goodness Grandee, and was granted the crimson fish tally.

sentences.zh: 唐同光初，遷大理正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang of Tang he was transferred to Senior Law Officer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tongguang of Tang he was promoted to Senior Law Officer of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，自將作少監轉大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was transferred from Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng he was transferred from Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 長興中，歷昭武、歸德兩鎮節度判官。

translations.literal: During Changxing he successively served as adjutant to the military commissioners of Zhaowu and Guide.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he served in turn as adjutant to the military commissioners of Zhaowu and Guide.

sentences.zh: 四年，復入為大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again entered court as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to court as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，除殿中監。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he was appointed Director of the Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he was appointed Director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 天福五年，拜大理卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Household for Food.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Household for Food.

sentences.zh: 仁願性溫雅，明法書，累居詳刑之地，議讞疑獄，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Renyuan's nature was gentle and refined; he understood law texts; he repeatedly held posts in detailed punishment, deliberated on doubtful cases, and was acclaimed as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan was gentle and refined by nature, versed in legal texts, and repeatedly held posts in judicial review. In deliberating doubtful cases he was widely regarded as thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 兄仁穎，梁朝仕至諸衛將軍，中年以風恙廢於家凡十餘年，仁願事之，出告反面，如嚴父焉，士大夫推為孝友。

translations.literal: His elder brother Renying rose in Liang service to General of the Various Guards; in midlife, afflicted by wind ailment, he was disabled at home for more than ten years; Renyuan served him, reporting when going out and returning when coming in, as to a strict father; scholar-officials praised him as filial and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Renying had risen under the Liang to General of the Various Guards, but in midlife was disabled at home by wind paralysis for more than ten years. Renyuan served him with the deference due a strict father, reporting when he went out and returning when he came in, and scholar-officials praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 仁穎善理家，勤而且約，婦女衣不曳地，什物多歷年所，如新市焉。

translations.literal: Renying was skilled at managing the household, diligent and frugal; women's garments did not trail on the ground, and many household goods after years of use were still like newly purchased.
translations.idiomatic: Renying was skilled at managing the household with diligence and thrift. Women's garments did not trail on the ground, and many household goods looked newly purchased even after years of use.

sentences.zh: 仁願開運元年再為大理卿，時隰州刺史王澈犯贓，朝廷以澈功臣之後，欲宥之，仁願累執奏不移，竟遣伏法，議者賞之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun Renyuan again became Director of the Court of Judicial Review; at that time Wang Che, prefect of Xi Prefecture, committed embezzlement; the court, because Che was descended from a meritorious minister, wished to pardon him; Renyuan repeatedly submitted firm memorials without yielding and in the end had him executed; commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiyun Renyuan again became Director of the Court of Judicial Review. When Wang Che, prefect of Xi Prefecture, was found guilty of embezzlement, the court wished to pardon him because he was descended from a meritorious minister. Renyuan submitted repeated firm memorials without yielding and ultimately had him executed, winning praise from commentators.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，以疾卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he died of illness, at age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun he died of illness at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈秘書監。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Director of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 趙熙，字績巨，唐宰相齊國公光逢之猶子也。

translations.literal: Zhao Xi, style Jiju, was the nephew of the Tang chief minister Duke of Qi, Guangfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xi, styled Jiju, was the nephew of the Tang chief minister Duke of Qi, Zhao Guangfeng.

sentences.zh: 起家授秘書省校書郎，唐天成中，累遷至起居郎。

translations.literal: He began his career appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat; during Tiancheng of Tang he was repeatedly promoted to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Proofreader in the Secretariat and during Tiancheng of Tang was successively promoted to Diarist.

sentences.zh: 數上章言事，以稱旨尋除南省正郎。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of state, and because his words accorded with the sovereign's intent he was soon appointed a regular director in the southern secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of state, and because his words pleased the emperor he was soon appointed a regular director in the southern secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天福中，承詔與張昭遠等修《唐史》，竟集其功。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he received an edict to compile the History of Tang together with Zhang Zhaoyuan and others, and in the end gathered the achievement to completion.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he received an edict to compile the History of Tang together with Zhang Zhaoyuan and others, and brought the project to completion.

sentences.zh: 開運中，自兵部郎中授右諫議大夫，賞筆削之功也。

translations.literal: During Kaiyun he was appointed from Director in the Ministry of War to Right Remonstrance and Policy Advisor, rewarding his editorial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyun he was promoted from Director in the Ministry of War to Right Remonstrance and Policy Advisor in reward for his editorial work.

sentences.zh: 及契丹犯闕，偽旨遣使於晉州率配豪民錢幣，以實行橐。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the capital, a forged edict dispatched an envoy to Jin Prefecture to levy and assign wealthy households' money and goods in order to fill the traveling stores.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded the capital, a forged edict dispatched an envoy to Jin Prefecture to levy money and goods from wealthy households in order to fill the traveling stores.

sentences.zh: 始受命之日，條制甚嚴，熙出衣冠族，性素輕急，既畏契丹峻法，乃窮理搜索，人甚苦之。

translations.literal: From the day he received the commission the regulations were very strict; Xi came from a cap-and-gown clan and was by nature light and hasty; fearing the Khitan's harsh laws, he exhaustively investigated and searched, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he received the commission the regulations were very strict. Xi came from a genteel family and was by nature impulsive. Fearing the Khitan's harsh laws, he searched exhaustively, and the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 及晉之三軍殺副使駱從朗，

translations.literal: When the three armies of Jin killed the deputy commissioner Luo Conglang,
translations.idiomatic: When the three armies of Jin killed the deputy commissioner Luo Conglang,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：契丹以節度副使駱從朗知晉州事，大將藥可儔殺從朗。）〉

translations.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror: The Khitan appointed the deputy military commissioner Luo Conglang to administer Jin Prefecture affairs; the great general Yao Kechou killed Conglang.)]
translations.idiomatic: (The Comprehensive Mirror: The Khitan appointed deputy military commissioner Luo Conglang to administer Jin Prefecture; the great general Yao Kechou killed Conglang.)]

sentences.zh: 百姓相率持仗害熙於館舍，識者傷之。

translations.literal: The common people in succession took up weapons and killed Xi at the guest house; the knowledgeable grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: The common people took up weapons in succession and killed Xi at the guest house, and those who understood the situation grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 李遐，兗州人也。

translations.literal: Li Xia was a man of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xia was a native of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少為儒，有節操。

translations.literal: From youth he was a Confucian scholar and had integrity of character.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was a Confucian scholar of firm integrity.

sentences.zh: 歷數鎮從事，及升朝，累遷尚書庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as staff officer in several garrisons, and when he rose to court was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer in several garrisons, and after entering court was successively promoted to Assistant Secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，以皇子重乂保釐洛邑，知遐強幹有守，除為西京留守判官，使之佐理，復重其廉勤，兼委監西京左藏庫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, because the prince Chongyi was appointed to guard and oversee Luoyang, knowing that Xia was strong, capable, and steadfast, he appointed him adjutant to the Western Capital garrison commander to assist in administration; he also valued his incorrupt diligence and concurrently entrusted him to supervise the Western Capital Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne the prince Chongyi was appointed to guard Luoyang. Recognizing Xia's strength, capability, and steadfastness, Gaozu appointed him adjutant to the Western Capital garrison commander to assist in administration, and also valued his incorrupt diligence by entrusting him to supervise the Western Capital Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 會張從賓作亂，使人輦取繒帛以賞群逆，遐曰：「不奉詔書，安敢承命！

translations.literal: When Zhang Congbin rebelled, he sent men to cart away silk and brocade to reward the rebels; Xia said: "Without receiving an imperial edict, how dare I accept the order!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Congbin rebelled he sent men to cart away silk and brocade to reward the rebels. Xia said: "Without an imperial edict, how dare I obey such an order!

sentences.zh: 」遂為其下所害。

translations.literal: " He was therefore killed by their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: " He was therefore killed by their men.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘆惜，賻贈加等，仍贈右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of this he sighed in regret, increased the funeral gifts by one grade, and also posthumously granted him Right Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard of this he sighed in regret, increased the funeral gifts by one grade, and posthumously granted him Right Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.

sentences.zh: 其母田氏，封京兆郡太君，仍給遐所食月俸，終母餘年。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Tian, was enfeoffed Lady of Jingzhao Commandery, and was still granted the monthly salary Xia had received until the end of her remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Tian, was enfeoffed Lady of Jingzhao Commandery and continued to receive Xia's monthly salary for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 其子俟服闋與官。

translations.literal: His son was to receive office after the mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: His son was to receive an official appointment after the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 後又遣兗州節度使李從溫就其舊業，賜牲幣綿帛等物，以旌其忠也。

translations.literal: Later the military commissioner of Yan Prefecture, Li Congwen, was also dispatched to visit his former home and grant sacrificial animals, silk gifts, cotton cloth, and other items to honor his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Later the military commissioner of Yan Prefecture, Li Congwen, was dispatched to visit Xia's former home and grant sacrificial animals, silk gifts, cotton cloth, and other items in honor of his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 尹玉羽，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Yin Yuyu was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yuyu was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 唐天福中，隨計京師，甚有文稱。

translations.literal: During Tianfu of Tang he went to the capital for the examination and had a great literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu of Tang he traveled to the capital for the examination and enjoyed a strong literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 會有苴杖之喪，累歲羸疾，冬不釋菅屨，期不變倚廬。

translations.literal: He happened to enter mourning with staff for a distant relative; for years he was weak and ill, in winter never putting aside straw sandals, and throughout the mourning period never leaving the mourning hut.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning with staff for a distant relative he was weak and ill for years, never putting aside his straw sandals even in winter and never leaving the mourning hut throughout the prescribed period.

sentences.zh: 制闋，隱居杜門，無仕宦之意。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he lived in seclusion behind closed doors and had no intention of seeking office.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he lived in seclusion behind closed doors with no wish to seek office.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，劉鄩辟為保大軍節度判官，歷雍、汴、滑、兗從事。

translations.literal: During Zhenming of Liang, Liu Yun recruited him as adjutant to the Baoda Army military commissioner; he successively served as staff officer in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenming of Liang, Liu Yun recruited him as adjutant to the Baoda Army military commissioner, and he later served as staff officer in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan in turn.

sentences.zh: （案：以下有闕。

translations.literal: (Note: There is a lacuna below.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: There is a lacuna below.

sentences.zh: 考宋黎持《移石經紀》：石經舊在務本坊，自天祐中韓建築新城，而石經委棄於野。

translations.literal: Examining Song Lichi's Record of Moving the Stone Classics: The stone classics formerly stood in Wuben Ward; from Tianyou onward Han Jian built the new city, and the stone classics were abandoned in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Song Lichi's Record of Moving the Stone Classics: The stone classics formerly stood in Wuben Ward, but from Tianyou onward Han Jian built a new city and the stone classics were abandoned in the wilds.

sentences.zh: 至朱梁時，劉鄩守長安，從幕吏尹玉羽之請，輦入城中，置於此地，即唐尚書省之西隅也。）〉

translations.literal: By the time of the Later Liang, Liu Yun was guarding Chang'an; at the request of his staff officer Yin Yuyu he had them carted into the city and placed at this site, namely the western corner of the Tang Secretariat.)]
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the Later Liang, Liu Yun was guarding Chang'an and, at the request of his staff officer Yin Yuyu, had them carted into the city and placed at this site—the western corner of the Tang Secretariat.)]

sentences.zh: 唐清泰中，為光祿少卿，退歸秦中，以林泉詩酒自樂，自號自然先生。

translations.literal: During Qingtai of Tang he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household for Food, retired to Qinzhong, and amused himself with forests, springs, poetry, and wine, styling himself Master Natural.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai of Tang he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household for Food, then retired to Qinzhong and amused himself with forests, springs, poetry, and wine, styling himself Master Natural.

sentences.zh: 宰臣張延朗手書而召，高臥不從，謂人曰：「庶孽代宗，不可仕也。

translations.literal: The chief minister Zhang Yanlang summoned him by personal letter, but he lay high and did not comply, saying to others: "An illegitimate scion has replaced the ancestral line—one cannot serve.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yanlang summoned him by personal letter, but he refused to rise, saying: "An illegitimate scion has usurped the ancestral line—one cannot serve such a ruler.

sentences.zh: 」及高祖入洛，即受詔而來，以所著《自然經》五卷貢之，且告其老。

translations.literal: " When Gaozu entered Luoyang he immediately accepted the edict and came, presenting the five volumes of his Natural Classic and also informing them of his old age.
translations.idiomatic: " When Gaozu entered Luoyang he accepted the summons at once, presented the five volumes of his Natural Classic, and informed the court of his advanced age.

sentences.zh: 即日璽書褒美，頒其器幣，授少府監致仕，月給俸錢及冬春二時服。

translations.literal: That same day an imperial letter praised him, bestowed ceremonial vessels and gifts, appointed him Vice Director of the Palace Stores with retirement, and granted monthly salary and winter and spring seasonal garments.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an imperial letter praised him, bestowed ceremonial gifts, appointed him Vice Director of the Palace Stores with retirement, and granted him monthly salary plus winter and spring seasonal garments.

sentences.zh: 天福中，卒，有《武庫集》五十卷行於世。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he died; his Armory Collection in fifty volumes circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he died. His Armory Collection in fifty volumes circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 鄭雲叟，本名遨，雲叟其字也，以唐明宗廟諱，故世傳其字焉，本南燕人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Yunsou, original name Ao—Yunsou was his style; because of the taboo on Emperor Mingzong of Tang's temple name, the world therefore transmitted his style—was originally a man of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunsou, whose original name was Ao and whose style was Yunsou—because of the taboo on Emperor Mingzong of Tang's temple name the world knew him by his style—was originally a native of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 少好學，耿介不屈。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and was upright and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and was upright and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗朝，嘗應進士舉，不第，因欲攜妻子隱於林壑，其妻非之，不肯行，雲叟乃薄遊諸郡，獲數百緡以贍其家，辭訣而去。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he once entered the jinshi examination and failed; he therefore wished to take his wife and children to hide in forests and valleys; his wife disapproved and refused to go; Yunsou then traveled lightly through various prefectures, obtained several hundred strings of cash to support his family, and took leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he took the jinshi examination and failed. He wished to take his wife and children to live in seclusion in the mountains, but his wife refused. Yunsou then traveled through various prefectures, earned several hundred strings of cash to support his family, and departed after bidding farewell.

sentences.zh: 尋入少室山，著《擬峰詩》三十六章，以導其趣，人多傳之。

translations.literal: Soon he entered Mount Shaoshi, composed thirty-six chapters of Peak-Mimicking Poems to express his inclinations, and many people transmitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered Mount Shaoshi and composed thirty-six chapters of Peak-Mimicking Poems to express his inclinations, and many people copied and circulated them.

sentences.zh: 後妻以書達意，勸其還家，雲叟未嘗一覽，悉投於火，其絕累如此。

translations.literal: Later his wife sent a letter conveying her thoughts and urging him to return home; Yunsou never once looked at it and threw it all into the fire—such was his cutting off of entanglements.
translations.idiomatic: Later his wife sent a letter urging him to return home. Yunsou never even opened it and threw it into the fire—such was his resolve to cut off all worldly ties.

sentences.zh: 俄聞西嶽有五鬛松，淪脂千年，能去三屍，因居於華陰。

translations.literal: Before long he heard that the Western Peak had a five-lobed pine whose oozing resin was a thousand years old and could expel the three corpses; he therefore settled at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he heard that the Western Peak had a five-lobed pine whose thousand-year resin could expel the three corpse-worms, and he therefore settled at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 與李道殷、羅隱之友善，時人目為「三高士」。
