translations.literal: He was friendly with Li Daoyin and Luo Yinshi, and people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Li Daoyin and Luo Yinshi, and people of the time called them the "Three High Recluses."

sentences.zh: 道殷有釣魚之術，鉤而不餌，又能化易金石，無所不至，雲叟恒目睹其事，信而不求。

translations.literal: Daoyin had the art of fishing with hook but no bait, and could also transform and transmute metal and stone—there was nothing he could not do; Yunsou constantly witnessed these things with his own eyes, believed but did not seek them.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyin could fish with a hook but no bait and could transform metal and stone—there seemed nothing beyond his art. Yunsou witnessed these things often, believed in them, but never sought them for himself.

sentences.zh: 雲叟與梁室權臣李振善，振欲祿之，拒而不諾，及振南遷，雲叟千里徒步以省之，識者高焉。

translations.literal: Yunsou was on good terms with Li Zhen, the powerful minister of the Liang court; Zhen wished to grant him salary, but he refused and did not consent; when Zhen moved south, Yunsou walked a thousand li on foot to visit him, and the knowledgeable held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsou was on good terms with Li Zhen, the powerful minister of the Liang court. When Zhen wished to grant him an official salary Yunsou refused, but when Zhen moved south Yunsou walked a thousand li on foot to visit him, and those who understood such things held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 後妻兒繼謝，每聞兇服，一哭而止。

translations.literal: Later his wife and children died in succession; whenever he heard of mourning garments he wept once and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later his wife and children died in succession. Whenever he heard that someone was in mourning he wept once and stopped.

sentences.zh: 時惟青衿二童子、一琴、一鶴，從其遊處。

translations.literal: At that time only two blue-collared boys, one zither, and one crane accompanied him in his wanderings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only two boys in blue collars, a zither, and a crane accompanied him wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 好棋塞之戲，遇同侶則以晝繼夜，雖寒風大雪，臨檐對局，手足皸裂，亦無倦焉。

translations.literal: He loved the game of qisai; when he met companions he played day into night; even in bitter wind and heavy snow, facing each other under the eaves, with hands and feet cracked and split, he never grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the board game qisai and, when he found companions, would play day into night. Even in bitter wind and heavy snow, playing under the eaves with cracked hands and feet, he never grew weary.

sentences.zh: 唐天成中，召拜左拾遺，不起。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng of Tang he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng of Tang he was summoned as Left Reminder but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 與羅隱之朝夕遊處，隱之以藥術取利，雲叟以山田自給，俱好酒能詩，善長嘯。

translations.literal: He spent his days and nights in companionship with Luo Yinshi; Yinshi made profit through pharmaceutical arts, while Yunsou supported himself from mountain fields; both loved wine and could compose poetry, and were skilled at long whistling.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days with Luo Yinshi. Yinshi made a living through pharmaceutical arts while Yunsou supported himself from mountain fields. Both loved wine, wrote poetry, and were skilled at long whistling.

sentences.zh: 有大瓠，雲可辟寒暑，置酒於其中，經時味不壞，日攜就花木水石之間，一酌一詠。

translations.literal: He had a large gourd said to ward off cold and heat; he placed wine in it and after a long time the flavor did not spoil; daily he carried it among flowers, trees, water, and stones, sipping and composing verse.
translations.idiomatic: He had a large gourd said to ward off cold and heat. He kept wine in it and even after a long time the flavor did not spoil. Each day he carried it among flowers, trees, water, and stones, sipping wine and composing verse.

sentences.zh: 嘗因酒酣聯句，鄭曰：「一壺天上有名物，兩個世間無事人。

translations.literal: Once, when wine had warmed them, they linked verses; Zheng said: "One pot—a famous thing from Heaven; two men—carefree people in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Once, deep in their cups, they linked verses in turn. Zheng said: "One pot—a famous thing from Heaven; two men—carefree souls in the world.

sentences.zh: 」羅曰：「醉卻隱之、雲叟外，不知何處是天真。

translations.literal: " Luo said: "When drunk, apart from Yinshi and Yunsou, one knows not where true innocence lies.
translations.idiomatic: " Luo replied: "When drunk, apart from Yinshi and Yunsou, who knows where true innocence lies?

sentences.zh: 」高祖即位，聞其名，遣使賫書致禮，征為右諫議大夫，雲叟稱疾不起，上表陳謝。

translations.literal: " When Gaozu ascended the throne he heard of his name, dispatched an envoy bearing a letter and gifts, and summoned him as Right Remonstrance and Policy Advisor; Yunsou claimed illness and did not rise, submitting a memorial to express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " When Gaozu took the throne he heard of Yunsou's reputation, sent an envoy bearing a letter and gifts, and summoned him as Right Remonstrance and Policy Advisor. Yunsou pleaded illness and declined, submitting a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽表嘉之，賜近臣傳觀，尋賜號逍遙先生，以諫議大夫致仕，月給俸祿。

translations.literal: Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, granting the close ministers to pass it around for viewing; soon he bestowed the title Master Free Wanderer, retired him as Remonstrance and Policy Advisor, and granted monthly salary.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, having it circulated among his close ministers. Soon he granted Yunsou the title Master Free Wanderer, retired him as Remonstrance and Policy Advisor, and awarded him a monthly stipend.

sentences.zh: 雲叟好酒，嘗為《詠酒詩》千二百言，海內好名者書於縑緗，以為贈貺。

translations.literal: Yunsou loved wine and once composed the Ode to Wine in twelve hundred words; fame-seekers throughout the realm copied it on silk and used it as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsou loved wine and once composed the "Ode to Wine" in twelve hundred words. Fame-seekers throughout the realm copied it onto silk and gave it as gifts.

sentences.zh: 復有越千里之外，使畫工潛寫其形容列為屏障者焉。

translations.literal: There were also those from more than a thousand li away who sent painters to secretly sketch his likeness and set it up as a screen.
translations.idiomatic: Some even came from more than a thousand li away, sending painters to secretly sketch his likeness and display it on a screen.

sentences.zh: 其為時望所重也如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held by the expectations of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 天福末，以壽終，時年七十四。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianfu he died a natural death, at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Tianfu he died peacefully at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works in twenty volumes circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in twenty volumes circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自古攀龍鱗，附鳳翼，坐達於雲衢者，豈獨豐沛之士哉！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: From antiquity those who climbed dragon scales and attached themselves to phoenix wings, reaching the cloud highways while seated—were they only men of Feng and Pei!
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: From antiquity, those who rose by grasping the dragon's scales and attaching themselves to the phoenix's wings, reaching the heights of power without struggle—were they found only among the men of Feng and Pei?

sentences.zh: 茍懷才抱器，適會興王，亦可以取貴於一時，如盧質而下數君子是也。

translations.literal: If one harbors talent and carries capacity, and happens to meet a rising sovereign, one may also gain honor for a time—such were the several gentlemen from Lu Zhi downward.
translations.idiomatic: If one harbors talent and meets a rising sovereign, one may also win honor for a time—such were the several gentlemen from Lu Zhi on down.

sentences.zh: 至如國珍之讜直，仁願之友悌，趙、李二子沒於王事，皆無忝於士林矣。

translations.literal: As for Guozhen's forthright integrity, Renyuan's fraternal devotion, and the two men Zhao and Li who perished in royal service—all were without disgrace to the forest of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: As for Guozhen's blunt integrity, Renyuan's fraternal devotion, and Zhao and Li who died in the service of the state—all did honor to the community of scholars.

sentences.zh: 唯玉羽之貞退，雲叟之肥遁，足可以柅奔競之風，激高尚之節也。

translations.literal: Only Yuyu's steadfast withdrawal and Yunsou's ample reclusion were sufficient to check the wind of frantic competition and inspire lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yuyu's steadfast withdrawal and Yunsou's ample reclusion were enough to check the rush of frantic ambition and inspire a higher standard of integrity.
